sections.heading: PQ Devnet-0 Status and Key Loading Bottleneck
sections.summary: Local devnets run with Lighthouse and Lodestar; compact key loading (leanVM PR 802) needed by all clients to scale past a few validators.
sections.body:
- Barnabas has been testing locally but is blocked by the lack of compact key loading: without it, importing validator keys takes minutes to hours, making local Kurtosis runs impractical beyond a handful of validators.
  - Default behavior loads 2^31 (4.3 billion) signing keys upfront; Emile's PR 802 loads only what's needed for roughly the next thousand slots or epochs.
  - Two competing PRs exist: [leanVM PR 802](https://github.com/leanEthereum/leanVM/pull/802) (from Emile/Tom Wambsgans) and [leanVM PR 794](https://github.com/leanEthereum/leanVM/pull/794).
- Agreement: clients should target PR 802 as the approach to implement; Barnabas and ethDreamer noted it is a client implementation change, not a spec change.
- Nimbus still uses the old spec with 2^20 leaves; Barnabas is fixing this in a separate branch.
- Lighthouse and Lodestar interop confirmed working locally with a small number of validators.
- Barnabas ran a 1,000-validator network but observed no aggregation happening; Lighthouse (ethDreamer) stated aggregation should be implemented but has not been tested at that scale. Barnabas believes aggregation only begins above ~512 validators.
- 10,000 pre-minted keys are now available in the ethereum-package for the default mnemonic.
- ethDreamer (Lighthouse) is actively implementing PR 802 with the goal of enabling 1,000+ validator devnets.
- ethlambda reported a working pq-devnet-0 branch with final test runs expected later that day.
- For Teku, Paul is working on pq-devnet-0 but not yet interoperating; not considering separated VC-BN for now.
- Prysm (terence) is making slow progress; working on figuring out the Beacon API between BN and VC.

sections.heading: Sync and Spec Open Questions
sections.summary: Clients should assume genesis-only starts for now; sync and checkpoint sync deferred to later devnets.
sections.body:
- terence asked whether clients need to implement block syncing and payload syncing for the devnet.
- Decision: assume always starting from genesis for now; no syncing required. Checkpoint sync and block sync will be addressed in later devnet iterations.
- Barnabas noted that without sync support, new clients cannot be onboarded to an already-running devnet, suggesting waiting until more clients are ready before launching.
- Justin Traglia countered that devnet-0 is still valuable for testing aggregation times, network propagation, and proposer proof merging even without sync.
- ethDreamer asked whether the upcoming devnet includes the "commit to VRF secrets instead of revealing leaves" spec change; Justin said not yet—a new commit will be posted for clients next week after progress on the current devnet.

sections.heading: Beacon API for PQ Validator Client
sections.summary: Ignacio to own a PQ branch of the Beacon API spec; short-term clients may copy Lighthouse's approach.
sections.body:
- Barnabas raised the need for a Beacon API spec for the VC ↔ BN interface under PQ.
- Justin Traglia proposed creating a PQ branch for Beacon APIs; Ignacio (not on the call) was assigned ownership.
- Luca (Vero) argued Beacon API changes are not worth speccing before determining if PQ Gasper is feasible, since decoupled consensus (DC) would require relatively bigger API changes.
  - Barnabas and others countered that PQ Gasper API changes may be small enough to spec now.
- terence (Prysm) asked for a Beacon API PR to follow; Barnabas suggested copying whatever Lighthouse implemented and iterating later.
- terence preferred a minimal approach now, with bikeshedding deferred.
- Multiple clients (Prysm, Lodestar, Lighthouse) cannot run validators inside the BN process, so VC interop eventually needs speccing; cayman noted this is forward-looking to future devnet requirements.

sections.heading: Staggered Aggregation Proposal
sections.summary: Justin Traglia implemented Potuz's staggered aggregation idea; 4 aggregators broadcast 500ms apart with delayed proposer inclusion.
sections.body:
- Justin Traglia implemented staggered aggregations in the [PQ validator spec](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/pq/specs/_features/pq/validator.md#construct-aggregate): 4 aggregators per committee stop collecting attestations and broadcast at different times, 500ms apart.
- Proposers get an entire additional slot to merge aggregates into their block proof (min attestation-inclusion delay change).
- Mikhail noted the table leaves about 2.4 seconds to produce an aggregate, and that staggering could also happen naturally due to varying CPU capabilities across aggregators.
- Justin clarified the key design choice: the cutoff time for attestation collection differs per aggregator, not just the broadcast time.
- Kamil confirmed aggregators aggregate whatever they have at the cutoff, with no threshold requirement.
- Kev asked whether the announce-then-pull approach (sending bitlist first, nodes pull the ~300KB proof) was abandoned; Kamil said it depends on the networking protocol chosen.
- Feedback was generally positive but acknowledged as early-stage.

sections.heading: LeanVM Aggregation Benchmarks on NUC
sections.summary: 16-to-1 aggregation takes ~3.5s on a NUC with 4 cores; allocating 6 performance cores brings it to 2 seconds.
sections.body:
- Tom Wambsgans reproduced Potuz's benchmarks on a NUC 14 Pro: 3.5 seconds for 16-to-1 aggregation without EL running; adding EL adds 10–20%.
  - The NUC has 6 efficiency cores and 2 performance cores; initial split was 3E+1P for leanVM and the same for EL.
  - With 6 performance cores allocated to leanVM and the EL on the remaining cores, aggregation drops to about 2 seconds; Tom put the numbers in the Discord thread.
- Csaba cautioned against over-interpreting microbenchmarks: real nodes run many concurrent tasks, and production environments vary widely (data center vs. home staker). Summer heat, thermal throttling, and power budgets add margins not captured in benchmarks.
- Dustin echoed that per-core tuning to specific P/E core layouts is fragile and would effectively rule out slower machines.
- Justin Traglia acknowledged benchmarks will be slower in production but emphasized the need for concrete numbers.
- Tom posted detailed results in the "Aggregation Benchmarks" thread on Discord (PQCL channel).
- Toni Wahrstätter noted the EL will also demand more resources with mempool aggregation; worst cases on both layers must be handled simultaneously.

sections.heading: Networking: Gossipsub vs. Waggle/Seacast
sections.summary: Gossipsub is too bandwidth-heavy for large PQ aggregates; Waggle+seacast implementations are progressing in Lighthouse and Prysm.
sections.body:
- Kamil's simulations show gossipsub is ~15% slower and uses ~7× more bandwidth than naive announce-and-pull for proof broadcast; bandwidth spikes of 200–300 Mbps observed for aggregation traffic alone, far exceeding EIP-7870 limits.
- Csaba confirmed gossipsub pushes aggressively, wasting bandwidth; newer protocols using advertise-and-pull with segmented broadcasting achieve a 2–3× bandwidth reduction.
- Waggle provides the low-level transport freeing clients from gossipsub limitations; seacast is the application-layer protocol on top defining the actual broadcast behavior.
  - Csaba has a seacast-on-waggle implementation running for Prysm, still to be checked against Prysm itself.
  - Kamil confirmed Lighthouse has an [EIP-8411](https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1572297783359180801) implementation with waggle that could be ported for proof messages.
  - vlad is working on [seacast-rs](https://github.com/gattaca-com/seacast-rs) (Rust implementation) running in a fork of silver CL.
  - Anton (Mikhail's team) vibecoded a seacast implementation but got worse-than-gossipsub results; acknowledged results may be unreliable and need checking.
- Kev pushed for speedrunning to waggle+segmented broadcasting since gossipsub is confirmed insufficient; Csaba and Kamil agreed but emphasized using gossipsub as a baseline for A/B comparison.
- Barnabas proposed dual-stack A/B testing on devnets (run both gossipsub and waggle, expose metrics via Prometheus); Csaba clarified waggle alone is just a pipe—a protocol on top is needed.
- Decision: first devnets will use gossipsub as baseline; waggle+seacast devnets to follow once implementations are ready (Kamil estimated Lighthouse with segmented proofs broadcast within a week, devnet the week after).
- Barnabas expressed frustration at repeated back-and-forth on gossipsub vs. waggle and asked the networking team to make a definitive decision.

sections.heading: Network Simulation Results (Mikhail/Anton)
sections.summary: Gossipsub simulation with 800K validators and D=4 shows attester nodes at bandwidth capacity; aggregates arrive P99 at 11.7s into the slot.
sections.body:
- Mikhail shared Anton's simulation setup: 800K validators, 16 subnets, 2 aggregators per subnet (minimum reasonable), aggregation due at 6 seconds, attestation size ~1,200 bytes, aggregate size 200KB, gossipsub with D=4.
  - ~1,000 nodes with distribution: ~100 home/attester nodes, hundreds of supernodes, rest in between.
  - Attester nodes not subscribed to backbone; middle nodes subscribed to 1 subnet; supernodes to 2+.
- Key findings:
  - Attester nodes receive P99 aggregates at 11.7 seconds into a slot—at bandwidth capacity, with some aggregates leaking into the next slot.
  - Local block builder nodes are fine: P99 at 8 seconds, not at capacity.
  - 3–4 seconds available for attestation receipt + aggregate computation, fitting current benchmarks but leaving CPU at capacity during aggregation.
- Possible mitigations discussed: increase bandwidth requirements, increase CPU requirements, reduce validator count via consolidation, switch PubSub protocol, increase slot times.
  - Mikhail's personal preference: not increase bandwidth or CPU requirements, not increase slot times.
  - terence raised concern about builder attestation observation assumptions needing revisiting under PQ timing constraints.
- Csaba noted the difference between push (gossipsub) and pull approaches has a factor of 2–3× in bandwidth; also emphasized uplink/downlink asymmetry as a tuning lever.
- Both Mikhail/Anton and Csaba agreed to publish detailed simulation results for cross-checking; acknowledged the importance of validating each other's setups.

sections.heading: PQ Registration System Contract and Migration
sections.summary: PQ registration contract updated with XMSS signature verification; migration happens at the PQ fork, not before.
sections.body:
- Justin Traglia and Ignacio updated the EIP to add XMSS signature verification to the PQ registration system contract; cost estimated at ~10 cents at current gas prices.
- Working system contract exists in the [pq-staking-contracts repository](https://github.com/ethereum/pq-staking-contracts).
- PQ registrations would be introduced at H-star (pre-PQ fork), allowing validators/builders to register PQ keys; at the PQ fork, all validators transition to PQ keys and the registration contract is deleted.
- PQ registrations are separate from validator pre-registrations and are not part of pq-devnet-0.
- Manu agreed to take on ERCs for VRF tree specification/generation and also the 2333/2334/2335 analogues (key derivation, storage, and mnemonic specs for PQ).

sections.heading: 0x02 Credential Requirement and Validator Consolidation
sections.summary: Proposal to disallow new 0x00 and 0x01 validators at H-star to push consolidation; concerns raised about whether it actually forces consolidation.
sections.body:
- Barnabas proposed disallowing new 0x00 and 0x01 validator deposits at H-star, requiring only 0x02 credentials, which would force existing 0x01 holders to migrate and potentially consolidate.
  - Best case: validator count could drop from 800K to ~54K (same withdrawal credential consolidation) or below 100K, potentially eliminating the need for recursive aggregation.
  - [EIP-8502](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-8502-dynamic-individual-consolidation-incentive/30436) (dynamic individual consolidation incentive) proposed by Anders Elowsson as a complementary mechanism; a capping EIP also in preparation.
- Pushback from NodeSet (staking operation) discussed; Barnabas argued their concerns would be resolved if EIP-8148 (custom sweep threshold) is included in H-star, since operators could then consolidate while keeping 32 ETH behaviour.
- Kev and Justin questioned whether forcing 0x02 actually leads to consolidation—people may do the minimum required work. Outreach to top staking entities suggested.
- NC pointed out 0x01 is fundamentally different from 0x00: force-exiting 0x01 validators refunds ETH to the execution address (no burn), so accepting and then force-exiting 0x01 deposits is not harmful.
- Luca noted Rocket Pool may not be ready for 0x02-only migration; StakeWise already supports 0x02.
- Francesco D'Amato cautioned that increasing slots per epoch to reduce aggregation load would be very complex; at that point, decoupled consensus or capping the validator set would be better.
- Dustin argued the decision should not rely on hoping people consolidate; the 0x02-only approach must work regardless.
- Decision deferred to async discussion; no consensus reached.

sections.heading: 0x00 Validators Who Lost Keys
sections.summary: Funds from 0x00 validators with lost keys could be sent to an EL contract recoverable by the original depositor; no consensus reached.
sections.body:
- Justin Traglia raised the question of what to do with 0x00 BLS validators who have lost their keys; acknowledged there may be nothing we can do.
- Ben Edgington proposed moving funds to an EL contract where the original depositing account can claim them, based on on-chain deposit history.
  - [HackMD writeup](https://hackmd.io/jW1q4xIDT5S2PJewFeatzA) shared by Ben.
  - A "DAO Fund" has proposed to manage validation of lost-key claims beyond simple account signatures; exists as an ETH Magicians post.
- NC argued this amounts to preferential treatment for a small group baked into the protocol; no equivalent rescue exists for other lost keys.
- Barnabas noted 0x00 validators never had withdrawal functionality (should have been available at the merge), so the situation is arguably already unfair.
- Justin Traglia supported the idea for validators who simply forgot to register PQ keys (still have their BLS keys) but was less sure about truly lost keys.
- Kev suggested this is not blocking and can be tackled later.
- Decision deferred to async; Barnabas noted it would involve an irregular state change, potentially implementable as a system contract.

sections.heading: Devnet Subnet Sizing and Measurement Methodology
sections.summary: Proposal to make subnet count configurable via config.yaml so smaller devnets can simulate mainnet-sized subnets; targeting devnet-1.
sections.body:
- Barnabas proposed running ~10,000 validators but overriding the number of subnets (e.g., fewer than 16) to match mainnet validator-per-subnet ratios, enabling meaningful aggregation testing without massive infrastructure.
- ethDreamer (Lighthouse) agreed this is probably the best approach for investigating aggregation times; noted the subnet count is currently derived from a formula (not a simple config), so a code modification is needed.
- Justin Traglia volunteered to look into adding a configurable subnet count to config.yaml; if not done in time, someone else can pick it up next week.
- Decision: save this for devnet-1; devnet-0 will launch with default parameters and smaller scale.
- Yann cautioned that scaling down is easy but interpreting results is hard—aggregation traffic patterns differ significantly at smaller scale.
- Csaba agreed this is a key differentiator between simulations and testnets.

sections.heading: Call Scheduling
sections.summary: Three calls per week retained for now; Tuesday preferred over Friday; Kev to moderate next week during Justin's Thanksgiving absence.
sections.body:
- Discussion on whether to keep 3 calls/week (Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday) or reduce.
- Barnabas favored keeping all 3 to maximize progress before December holidays; acknowledged Friday attendance is low.
- Kev preferred fewer calls; suggested 2 per week.
- Multiple participants (soispoke, Justin, Enrico) expressed preference for the Tuesday call over Friday.
- Agreement: keep all 3 calls for now; end early if nothing to discuss. Kev will decide schedule next week.
- Justin Traglia will be out of office all of next week (Thanksgiving); Kev will moderate.
- Enrico noted Teku's Paul may have something for the APAC timezone.
